title: The Role of Neuroscience and Artificial Intelligence in Biophilic Architectural Design Based on the Principle of Symbiosis
review_question: To synthesise findings from the latest scientific journals on applying neuroscience and AI in biophilic architecture, focusing on improving human-natural connectivity based on the principle of symbiosis.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Peer-reviewed scientific journals, published in English between 2018-2023, substantially addressing the application of neuroscience and AI in biophilic architectural design, and focused on improving human-nature relations.

findings.antecedent: Multi-objective optimisation (façade design, natural lighting, energy efficiency, biophilic aesthetics)

They devised a façade design using evolutionary algorithms that balances some of these goals. These studies demonstrate the potential for Al to automate and optimise certain aspects of biophilic design and enable a more comprehensive exploration of design spaces and more optimal solutions.

findings.antecedent: Computer vision (detecting occupants' number and behavior)
findings.consequent: Adjustment of digital natural elements display to optimize biophilic experience

findings.quote: Mollazadeh et al. demonstrated a responsive installation that uses computer vision to detect the number and behaviour of occupants and adjust the display of digital natural elements to optimise the biophilic experience [21].

synthesis_conclusions: Neuroscience findings provide empirical evidence on the psychophysiological benefits of various biophilic design elements, guiding feature selection for targeted effects.
AI techniques (generative algorithms, deep learning, multi-objective optimisation) enable efficient exploration of vast design spaces, identifying optimal design solutions, and predictive modelling.

Integrating neuroscience and AI promises the creation of highly adaptive and responsive built environments that adapt to human circumstances and preferences in real time, improving well-being and sustainability.
A careful and responsible approach to neuroscience and AI can transform design, fostering a more harmonious and symbiotic relationship between humans, nature, and technology.
Biophilic architecture underpinned by neuroscience insights and AI capabilities can create habitats that promote holistic well-being and proactively adapt to changing environmental and human needs.
evidence_gaps: Need for further interdisciplinary research to refine methodologies, develop best practice guidelines, and advance visions of an intelligent, human-centred biophilic environment.
Methodological challenges in designing ecologically valid architectural neuroscience studies while controlling for confounding variables.
Ethical challenges related to privacy and consent in physiological and behavioural data collection.
Potential for bias in AI models to amplify inequalities if not critically examined.
Implications of overly prescriptive AI-driven design on human creativity and cultural adaptation.
limitations: Difficulties in designing ecologically valid architectural neuroscience studies while controlling for confounding variables.
Importance of standard protocols and reference data sets for neuroscience studies.
Potential for bias in AI models that could amplify inequalities if not critically examined.
Privacy and consent concerns regarding physiological and behavioural data collection.
Need for clear ethical guidelines to ensure responsible use of data and protect individual autonomy.
Concerns about overly prescriptive AI-driven design potentially reducing human creativity and cultural adaptation.
Need to balance optimisation with flexibility and openness in the design approach.
Further research and experimentation are required for applying neuroscience and AI in biophilic architecture.

paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Biophilic architecture aims to create an environment that enhances connectivity between humans and nature to improve physical, mental, and emotional well-being. This review analyses 25 recent scientific journals on the application of neuroscience and artificial intelligence (AI) to optimise biophilic architectural design based on the principle of symbiosis. Results show that neuroscience provides valuable insights into human psychophysiological responses to various biophilic elements, while AI enables complex data processing, predictive modelling, and real-time design adaptation. The collaboration of neuroscience and AI can help produce a more effective, responsive to human needs, and sustainable biophilic environment. On the other hand, flexibility is demonstrated by the breadth of the architectural design process phases that can be reached through this collaboration. However, methodological and ethical challenges must be addressed to ensure responsible application.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Humans possess an innate tendency to connect with nature and other living systems, which influences well-being.
Exposure to natural environments can restore directed attention capacity and reduce mental fatigue.
Viewing natural scenes can lead to rapid physiological stress reduction and positive emotional states.
Biophilic architectural design, informed by neuroscience and AI, should foster a mutually beneficial and integrated relationship between humans, nature, and technology.

mechanism_chain.description: Biophilic architectural elements, perceived through sensory systems, activate specific neural pathways, leading to physiological and cognitive benefits, potentially enhanced or monitored by AI.
